title: How many small parts make a bigger place?
description: Five counting questions about places are answered by counting the steps of ten between them: thousandths in a unit, in a tenth and in a hundredth, then tenths and hundredths in a ten. Keeko's doubt is that a unit and a thousandth are neighbours.
teaching_notes: One idea: each step between two places is a factor of ten, so count the steps and multiply ten that many times. Watch for students who treat distant places as neighbours and answer ten.

source: (a) How many thousandths make one unit? (b) How many make on
video_script.why: The child knows the ladder of places and now counts how many small parts fill a bigger place.
video_script.substitution: The number of small parts in a bigger place is ten multiplied once for each step between the two places.
video_script.anchor: the ladder of places from a ten down to a thousandth
video_script.wrong_move: treats a unit and a thousandth as neighbours, one step apart
video_script.payoff_line: Each step of ten multiplies the count by ten

final_answer.spoken: one thousand, one hundred, ten, one hundred and one thousand

video_script.fraction_reading: tenths, hundredths and thousandths are said as words
maths_rules: places in order: ten, unit, tenth, hundredth, thousandth; each step to the right divides a part into 10
unit to thousandth: 3 steps, 10 x 10 x 10 = 1000 thousandths in a unit
tenth to thousandth: 2 steps, 10 x 10 = 100 thousandths in a tenth
hundredth to thousandth: 1 step, 10 thousandths in a hundredth
a ten is 10 units and each unit is 10 tenths: 10 x 10 = 100 tenths in a ten
each tenth is 10 hundredths: 100 x 10 = 1000 hundredths in a ten
the slip: a unit and a thousandth are 3 steps apart, not 1
video_script.design: The ladder of places stays on the stage; arrows count the steps of ten between two places, the counts build in the working band, and Keeko's doubt shows three arrows against one.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book, then the ladder of places ten, unit, tenth, hundredth, thousandth; a question mark in the anchor band

marks.ladder: the ladder of places is drawn

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the sizes of places.
<bookmark mark='ladder'/>A ten, a unit, a tenth, a hundredth and a thousandth stand on a ladder.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many thousandths make one unit?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits beside it as the child
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the ladder 10, 1, 1/10, 1/100, 1/1000 with an arrow between each pair of places: each step right splits a part into 10

marks.steps: an arrow joins each pair of neighbouring places
marks.split: each arrow is marked split into 10

narration: <bookmark mark='steps'/>The places go in steps. Each step to the right is the place before it.
<bookmark mark='split'/>It is cut into ten equal parts, so every step multiplies the number of parts by ten.

beats.on_screen: Given: the places ten, unit, tenth, hundredth and thousandth
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the places ten, unit, tenth, hundredth and thousandth.

beats.on_screen: To find: thousandths in a unit, in a tenth, in a hundredth; tenths in a ten; hundredths in a ten
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how many thousandths make a unit, a tenth and a hundredth.
We also find how many tenths and how many hundredths make a ten.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: unit to thousandth is 3 steps: 10 x 10 x 10 = 1000; tenth to thousandth is 2 steps: 10 x 10 = 100; hundredth to thousandth is 1 step: 10

marks.unit: three arrows are counted from unit to thousandth
marks.tenth: two arrows from tenth to thousandth
marks.hundredth: one arrow from hundredth to thousandth

narration: <bookmark mark='unit'/>Step one, count the steps of ten. From a unit to a thousandth is three steps, so multiply ten by ten by ten.
<bookmark mark='tenth'/>From a tenth to a thousandth is two steps, so multiply ten by ten.
<bookmark mark='hundredth'/>From a hundredth to a thousandth is one step, so the count is ten.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: a ten is 10 units and each unit is 10 tenths: 10 x 10 = 100 tenths; each tenth is 10 hundredths: 100 x 10 = 1000 hundredths

marks.tenths: ten units, each with 10 tenths, are shown
marks.hundredths: each tenth is split into 10 hundredths

narration: <bookmark mark='tenths'/>Step two, go up to a ten. A ten is ten units, and each unit is ten tenths, so multiply ten by ten.
<bookmark mark='hundredths'/>Each tenth is ten hundredths, so we multiply that count by ten again.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 1000 thousandths in a unit, 100 in a tenth, 10 in a hundredth; 100 tenths and 1000 hundredths in a ten

marks.ans: the answers for the three small parts are boxed
marks.ten: the answers for the ten are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Each step of ten multiplies the count by ten.
A unit holds one thousand thousandths, a tenth holds one hundred, and a hundredth holds ten.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>A ten holds one hundred tenths and one thousand hundredths.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the ladder of places
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: one arrow unit to thousandth is struck out; three arrows are drawn and counted; 10 x 10 x 10 is written

marks.doubt: one arrow from unit to thousandth appears
marks.fix: the arrow is struck out and three arrows are drawn

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks ten thousandths make a unit, because a unit and a thousandth are neighbours.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But from a unit down to a thousandth there are three steps. Three steps of ten mean ten times ten times ten.
